assumptions: Assay compatibility: capture reagents and spike-in tracer are compatible with fractionation and elution buffers (assay-buffer interference ruled out by controls).
Material yield: sufficient particle-mass is recoverable to run spike-in and capture/protection assays at fraction level (n>=3 biological lots).

Spike-in behavior: chosen exogenous intact-EV tracer behaves in a manner representative of intact EVs (membrane-protected and capture-reactive) and is analytically distinguishable from endogenous signal.
biological_rationale: MISEV-style guidance and program preclinical evidence demonstrate that marker signals and functional effects can arise from non-vesicular co-isolates; a spike-in control plus membrane-protection readout distinguishes true membrane-protected, particle-associated signal from soluble/assay artifacts. Establishing a qualitative identity gate avoids asserting potency while enabling reproducible lot-gating for downstream CMC decisions.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail based on concurrent spike-in membrane-protected recovery + endogenous capture co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity across replicates.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Spike-in–validated intact-EV identity (qualitative pass/fail)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Controls for assay recovery and distinguishes membrane-protected particle-associated marker signal from soluble/assay artifacts without asserting potency.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: depends on spike-in choice and assay-buffer compatibility.

edges.competing_explanation: Spike-in could validate assay recovery while endogenous EV enrichment is absent (i.e., assay works but sample lacks intact EVs).
edges.missing_experiment: Blinded spike-in matrix to confirm that spike-in recovery tracks assay performance independent of endogenous signal.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal capture and membrane-protection controls but does not specify program-level spike-in designs; recovery may vary with spike-in choice and sample biomass.

edges.competing_explanation: A failed identity gate could reflect downstream exposure, formulation, or sampling sensitivity rather than intrinsic absence of EVs in the production lot.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recoverability study using only lots that pass the identity gate to confirm detectability in nasal lavage/CSF/tissue.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: large-animal intranasal lack-of-detection increases the operational need for a robust identity gate before bridging studies; absence of spike-in–validated endogenous signal may reflect delivery, labeling, or sample-sensitivity issues rather than identity alone.

nodes.statement: If an administered preparation contains a genuine membrane-protected, particle-associated EV population, then an exogenous intact-EV spike-in added before fractionation will be recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and will lose signal after detergent + protease/RNase (assay validation).

If endogenous capture-positive signal co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive in a bounded fraction but not in concentrated secretome controls, then the bounded fraction can be classified as EV-enriched for drug-substance definition (non-potency identity attribute).

If the bounded fraction fails to show spike-in–validated co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive endogenous capture signal across replicates, the preparation is analytically indistinguishable from secretome and should not be advanced as an EV-enriched drug-substance.

competing_explanations: Negative endogenous capture despite spike-in recovery may reflect sample-specific suppression of endogenous markers (e.g., epitope masking) rather than absence of EVs.
Apparent co-localization might reflect co-elution of non-vesicular particles bearing the same epitopes; detergent/protease protection helps discriminate but has limits.
dependencies: Select and QC an exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and validate capture-compatibility panels before assay interpretation
Produce >=3 independent pilot conditioned-medium lots with controlled pre-analytic handling
Establish SOPs for spike-in addition, fractionation windows, capture/elution buffers, and qualitative scoring rubric
design_question: Can a spike-in–controlled, orthogonal fraction-level workflow (exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery + intact-material immuno-capture co-localized with particle-peak fractions + detergent/protease protection) provide a reproducible qualitative pass/fail identity gate that distinguishes an EV-enriched bounded small-EV drug-substance candidate from a secretome-retaining concentrate, without implying potency?
expected_measurable_effect: Qualitative pass/fail classification per lot: EV-enriched (pass) when both spike-in membrane-protected recovery and endogenous capture-positive co-localization with detergent/protease sensitivity are reproducibly observed in particle-peak fractions across independent replicates; otherwise 'secretome-like (fail)'.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal, per-fraction workflow: (1) fractionate and measure particle counts per fraction; (2) intact immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture on fractions with separate readouts for spike-in tracer and endogenous markers; (3) protease/RNase +/- detergent on captured material; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (5) qualitative co-localization scoring across fractions.
experiment.comparator: Matched pair from the same conditioned-medium lot: (A) bounded small-EV fraction spiked with exogenous intact-EV tracer versus (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) spiked identically. Include detergent+protease-treated aliquots and buffer-only negative controls.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV preparation spiked into buffer and processed in parallel (validates capture and protection assay performance). Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples. Capture-compatibility buffer panels to rule out assay interference.
dependencies: Sufficient conditioned-medium yield across biological replicates
Validated spike-in reagent and capture-detection reagents with buffer-compatibility data
Access to particle-count instrumentation and fractionation equipment
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible endogenous capture-positive co-localization in bounded fractions across >=3 lots despite validated spike-in recovery, or inconsistent spike-in recovery preventing assay-controlled discrimination.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If spike-in recovery is confirmed but endogenous capture-positive co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive signal are not reproducibly observed in bounded fractions across independent lots, the hypothesis is falsified: treat material as secretome-like for identity/CMC decisions and pivot to alternate fractionation or secretome-centric strategies.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: An orthogonal identity gate consisting of exogenous intact-EV spike-in membrane-protected recovery co-localized with particle-count peaks plus endogenous capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive co-localization in bounded small-EV fractions (but not secretome controls) will discriminate EV-enriched drug-substance candidates from secretome-retaining material.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization: particle-count peak fractions that are capture-positive and show (A) preserved spike-in tracer signal that is lost after detergent+protease (validating assay recovery and membrane protection) and (B) endogenous capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive in bounded fraction but not in secretome control.
experiment.question: Does adding an exogenous intact-EV spike-in prior to fractionation enable qualitative discrimination between a bounded EV-enriched fraction and a concentrated secretome-retaining conditioned-medium by demonstrating (A) spike-in membrane-protected recovery co-localized with particle peaks and (B) endogenous capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive co-localization in the bounded fraction but not in secretome control?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed into: (A) bounded small-EV enrichment (e.g., SEC/iodixanol-bounded fraction) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) from the same lot
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) QC-characterized for particle counts and marker display
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV markers (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents) and separate tracer-detection reagents to distinguish spike-in
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane disruption controls
Density-fractionation materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative recovered & membrane-protected vs not recovered)
Protein:particle ratio differences between bounded fraction and secretome control
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n >= 3 independent conditioned-medium lots)
experiment.success_criterion: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, (1) the spike-in tracer is recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and shows loss after detergent+protease (validating assay recovery and membrane protection), and (2) endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior are reproducibly observed in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in the secretome-retaining concentrate processed identically. This pattern yields a qualitative pass/fail identity gate: bounded fraction = EV-enriched (pass); secretome = not EV-enriched (fail).

explicit_inferences: Inference: Spike-in recovery that is membrane-protected validates assay sensitivity; endogenous absence despite validated spike-in implies lack of intact-EV enrichment in that sample.
Inference: A qualitative identity gate avoids premature numeric release limits while enabling CMC go/no-go decisions and prioritizing bridging only for analytically validated EV-enriched lots.
falsification_criteria: Validated spike-in recovery (membrane-protected and recovered in particle-peak fractions) is observed but endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior are not reproducibly observed across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots; or

Spike-in recovery is inconsistent across replicates (preventing assay-controlled discrimination). Either outcome falsifies the hypothesis and requires treating the material as analytically indistinguishable from secretome for identity and CMC decisions.
human_decisions_required: Select spike-in tracer species/label and approve spike-in QC criteria
Select immuno-capture panel (which canonical epitopes and tracer assay) and approve capture/elution buffers
Authorize pilot-lot production volumes and acceptable pre-analytic handling SOPs
manufacturability_assessment: Feasible as a qualitative, non-numeric gate during Stage-1 manufacturing: requires production of several pilot lots and incorporation of a spike-in reagent into routine fractionation QC. Does not require validated numeric release criteria at this stage but requires SOPs for spike-in addition, capture/elution conditions, and fractionation windows.
manufacturing_rationale: A qualitative, pass/fail identity gate tied to orthogonal fraction-level evidence (spike-in recovery + capture co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity) provides a tractable, non-numeric manufacturing gate for choosing whether a lot should be advanced for scale-up, bridging, and potency-linkage work, avoiding premature numeric release specifications while de-risking wasted bridging studies.
measurement_strategy: Per-lot orthogonal fraction workflow: (A) add characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in to bulk conditioned medium before fractionation; (B) apply chosen fractionation (bounded small-EV candidate and secretome control from same lot); (C) collect density/size fractions and measure particle counts per fraction (NTA/TRPS); (D) perform intact-material immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture on fractions to detect spike-in tracer and endogenous markers separately; (E) apply protease+RNase +/- detergent to captured material to test membrane protection; (F) record qualitative co-localization (particle-peak fraction index vs capture signal) and spike-in behavior; (G) require reproducible pattern across >=3 lots to call pass.
novelty_statement: Novelty: This hypothesis commits to a concrete, spike-in–controlled, fraction-level identity gate (not proposed previously in the program material) that (A) uses an exogenous intact-EV tracer to validate per-sample assay recovery and membrane protection and (B) requires endogenous intact-material capture co-localization with particle-peak fractions plus detergent/protease sensitivity as a qualitative pass/fail criterion to classify a preparation as EV-enriched. This differs from prior proposals by making the spike-in an explicit within-sample control that enables a non-numeric, operational identity gate suitable for manufacturing go/no-go decisions (distinct from prior exploratory capture-only or particle-count–centric concepts).
principal_risks: Spike-in selection risk: an unsuitable spike-in (different stability or capture properties) could generate false validation signals (mitigate by orthogonal spike-in constructs and controls).
Assay interference risk: capture/elution or fractionation buffers may mask epitopes or interfere with detection (mitigate with buffer-compatibility panels).
Material-yield risk: low fraction biomass may prevent robust per-fraction assessment, limiting interpretability (mitigate by ensuring pilot lot volumes and concentrating where appropriate).
False-negative gate risk: a true EV-enriched lot could be misclassified if downstream handling (device/formulation exposure) occurs before assay—enforce consistent pre-analytic handling SOPs.
proposed_potency_relationship: None asserted. This identity gate is explicitly non-potency and is intended only to classify material for downstream CMC and bridging decisions.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a non-numeric orthogonal intact-EV identity gate (pass/fail) defined by: (A) per-sample recovery of an exogenous, characterized intact-EV spike-in that co-localizes with particle-count peaks in fractionation and is lost after detergent + protease/RNase (validating membrane protection and assay function); and (B) endogenous intact-material immuno-capture positive signal for canonical EV surface epitopes on the same particle-peak fractions that is substantially reduced or abolished after detergent + protease/RNase. Passing this gate classifies a preparation as 'EV-enriched (pass)'; failing it classifies the preparation as 'secretome-like (fail)'.
title: Spike-in–validated, fraction-level intact-EV identity gate to classify SGL-001 as an EV-enriched bounded drug-substance versus secretome-like material
